cues: A cook mashes soft fruit into pancake batter, adding sweetness without needing much extra sugar.
When the peel develops brown freckles, the fruit is often saved for quick bread rather than eaten plain.
A parent slices ripe pieces over oatmeal before packing breakfast for a child’s school day.
The blender turns frozen chunks, milk, and yogurt into a thick drink for an afternoon snack.
At a picnic, someone peels a portable snack and drops the empty skin into the compost bin.
A baker mashes overripe flesh into muffins, where its moisture helps keep the crumb tender.
Small pieces are stirred into cereal just before serving, so they stay tender instead of becoming soggy.
After peeling, a cook dips slices in batter and fries them until their edges turn golden.
